report:
Native liver, total hepatectomy

Received fresh is a native liver weighing 1380 g and measuring 23 x 16 x 9 cm. The hilar margins (bile duct, portal vein and hepatic artery) are submitted en face. The gallbladder is attached. Two hilar lymph nodes are identified. The liver is serially sliced at 5 mm intervals. The parenchyma is diffusely micronodular. Nodule 1, in segment 6, measures 20 mm and is necrotic, with a lipiodol-stained rim. Nodule 2, in segment 8, measures 25 mm and is tan, bulging, partly necrotic. All lesions described on imaging are identified. Representative sections are taken; see block key.

The liver shows established cirrhosis (Ishak stage 6/6) with mild interface and lobular activity. Nodule 1 (segment 6, 20 mm) is completely necrotic, with no viable tumour, consistent with treated hepatocellular carcinoma. Nodule 2 (segment 8, 25 mm) is a hepatocellular carcinoma with about 40% necrosis; the viable tumour measures 15 mm. Two hilar lymph nodes show reactive changes. The gallbladder shows chronic cholecystitis.

- Histologic grade: G2: Moderately differentiated
- Tumour histology:

- Tumour extension: Tumour confined to liver
